incident-bot: INCIDENT OPEN - Paging oncall: high error-rate spike in smart-routing with degraded outputs reported by customers. alert_id=INC-20260315-83

ashley (support): seeing ~30 support tickets where customers say the model is returning answers from a different model family (weird tokenization/format). High-severity for a financial customer.

sara (oncall): @mike @kevin are you able to jump in? Paging now. Any immediate mitigation?

mike: on it. pulling metrics. Looks like an uptick in model-mismatch errors concurrent with multiple region fallback events 09:12-09:18 UTC.

kevin: I’m 1min away. Quick read: routing logs show fallbacks from us-east -> eu-west for a subset of keys. Cache hit rates dropped, but error rate went up for rerouted requests.

ryan: logs sample: `route_decision: fallback(target=eu-west, reason=capacity)` and then `kv_cache_lookup: hit=true, key="prefix::gptx-3.2"` but the model actually served was `gptx-2.7-quant`. That looks wrong.

mike: that smell like cache key missing variant or region suffix. If cache keys are only model-name, a cached KV/prefix for model A in eu-west could be reused for model B in us-east after fallback.

jen: confirming: we have a recent rollout to change fallback routing policy (canary) that touched the cache-key schema in router config. I rolled the change through canary at 08:50 UTC.

ashley (support): customers impacted: acct-453 (finance), acct-991 (healthcare), and others low-volume but critical. They see misaligned completions, some PII redaction failures (we need to escalate).

sara (oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) disable the new fallback policy canary 2) invalidate affected KV prefixes 3) roll forward a fix to ensure cache key includes region+variant 4) monitor customer errors. Assigning tasks: @mike disable canary, @kevin invalidate cache prefixes, @ryan check logs/alerts, @jen prepare rollback patch.

mike: disabling canary now. `routing-service canary disable --id fallback-canary-20260315`

devops-bot: deploy status: canary disable request queued -> applied to 2/3 nodes -> applied to 5/5 nodes (ok).

mike: canary disabled. routing decisions should stop using new fallback pol.

kevin: running targeted cache invalidation for prefixes we believe are impacted. Command run:```
redwood cache invalidate --prefix "kv::model_cache::gptx" --regions all --confirm
```

kevin: invalidation kicked off. Expect propagation 30-60s.

ryan: starting synthetic checks against impacted customers' tenants now. Sending test completions and checking headers.

ashley (support): I told acct-453 we are investigating and taking mitigation steps; asked them to pause critical jobs until we confirm.

jen: preparing hotfix. Root cause confirmed: router config used `cache_key = "${model_name}"` in the canary. Should be `"${model_name}::${variant}::${region}"`. Patch ready: https://git.redwood/infra/router/changeset/PR-812

mike: can we hotpatch or do a normal deploy? We want minimal blast radius.

jen: it's a small templating change in the routing layer. I can build and roll a 2-node canary for the router with the corrected key. Will do canary->gradual.

devops-bot: cache invalidation completed across 8 clusters.

ryan: synthetic tests show completions back to expected model behavior for 90% requests. Latency stable. Error rate 5xx -> down to baseline.

sara (oncall): good. Ashley: can we start re-notifying customers with ETA? Keep them in outage status until we hit sustained 15m of green.

ashley (support): noted. Notifying acct-453 and acct-991 with status: mitigated, remediation in progress, will follow up in 1 hour.

mike: rolling router patch now. `kubectl rollout restart deploy/router --selector=canary=fix-cache-key`

devops-bot: rollout started: router patch PR-812 -> building -> image pushed -> canary nodes 1/2 updated.

kevin: monitoring KV caches. No more cross-region key reuse in logs. I still see a tiny tail where old cache entries might persist on long-lived workers; doing a targeted restart for those worker pools.

mike: canary healthy. Gradual roll to remaining router nodes.

devops-bot: rollout complete: 10/10 router pods updated. Health checks passed.

ryan: 30m after mitigation: error rates stabilized, customer-facing errors resolved per synthetic traces. Re-run of GTs shows correct model variant returned with appropriate tokenization.

ashley (support): acct-453 says job resumed, they reported result looks sane. They still want a postmortem.

sara (oncall): INCIDENT STATUS -> MITIGATED. Root cause: fallback policy canary introduced a truncated cache key that omitted variant+region, allowing cached KV/prefix entries to be reused across incompatible model variants and regions during fallback, leading to incorrect completions and PII redaction misses.

sara (oncall): ACTION ITEMS (short term): 1) postmortem + RCA 2) add unit/integration test for cache-key schema 3) extend canary checklist to include cache-key validation 4) add alert/guard when cache hit rate drops but error rate rises. Owners: jen (patch & tests), kevin (cache invalidation tooling), mike (canary checklist), ashley (customer comms).

mike: filing followup PRs now and will add automated linting to detect missing placeholders in router templates.

jen: I'll write the change and tests. Also will add a staged chaos test that simulates region fallback while validating cache isolation.

ryan: I'll bake an observability dashboard showing instance-level cache key composition and a rate alert for mismatch patterns.

ashley (support): I'll coordinate postmortem distribution and customer-facing timeline.

sara (oncall): thanks team. Closing incident thread once postmortem draft is linked.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED - mitigated at 1761235150. Duration ~11 minutes.
